security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG translates or executes any Integrated Matrix Extension instruction when the current vtype.vlmul CSR field encodes a fractional LMUL setting (MF2=0b001, MF4=0b010, MF8=0b011) without raising an illegal-instruction exception. This occurs in the per-instruction decode or translate phase where vtype.vlmul is not validated against the allowed set {1,2,4,8} for IME opcodes.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: target/riscv/insn_trans/trans_integrated_matrix.c.inc: translate-time or helper-time check missing for vlmul ∈ {MF2,MF4,MF8} before IME instruction execution; any path where require_vector(true) passes but require_vlmul_integral() or equivalent inline check is absent for matrix opcodes
affected_entities: all IME computational instructions (matrix multiply-accumulate variants)
security_spec.summary: QEMU must reject IME instructions when vlmul encodes fractional LMUL (MF2/MF4/MF8) by raising illegal-instruction, otherwise guest executes reserved behavior producing undefined matrix results

findings.finding: File does not exist in this QEMU tree. No Integrated Matrix Extension translation code is present, so no LMUL-integer check can be missing. The PR under review is an ISA spec change (src/integrated-matrix.adoc), not a QEMU implementation. No IME instructions are decoded or translated.
findings.snippet: (file not found — no IME implementation exists in this QEMU version)

findings.finding: No matrix opcode decode entries exist (no vmacc.m, vfwmacc.m, or similar IME instructions). The only matrix-related content is existing standard vector MACC entries (vmacc_vv, vwmacc_vv, vfwmacc_vv, etc.) which correctly allow fractional LMUL per the base V spec.
findings.snippet: (no IME decode entries — decode file has 0 occurrences of 'integrated', 'matrix', 'ime', or 'imat')

findings.finding: Existing vtype_reserved() correctly guards reserved bits (shift 8 for non-zvfbfa, shift 9 for zvfbfa). It does not — and should not — enforce IME-specific LMUL restrictions since no IME implementation exists. The vlmul & 4 fractional check at line 75 is correct for the base V extension.

Existing EMUL constraint helpers (require_align, require_noover) handle fractional LMUL (lmul < 0) correctly for the base V extension — fractional LMUL allows any register number. These helpers are not used for IME instructions because no IME instructions exist. If IME is added, new trans_ functions must explicitly reject fractional LMUL before reaching these helpers.
